samples.summary: Nested blockquote depth (`> > `, `>> `) is a documented capability of the new `QUOTE_RE`/`BARE_BOX_RE` but no test exercises depth > 1
samples.evidence: `QUOTE_RE = /^ {0,3}(?:> ?)+/` and `BARE_BOX_RE = /^( {0,3}(?:> ?)*\s*)\[([ xX])\]$/` explicitly admit repeated `>` markers, and the JSDoc names `'> > '` / `'>> '` as supported forms. Every new test in list-commands.test.ts (lines 40-74, 233-255, 276-283) and checkbox-input.test.ts (line 62) uses exactly one `> `. In particular `itemAbove`/`parentOf` compare quote prefixes by raw string equality (`prev.quote !== p.quote`, list-commands.ts:149,163), so `>> - a` followed by `> > - b` — same rendered depth — would be treated as different containers and nesting/outdent would silently stop working. Nothing asserts this, and the counters key `${p.quote} ${p.indent.length}` (line 279) has the same raw-string sensitivity.
searchedFor: grep for '> >' and '>>' in packages/notes/src/view tests

samples.summary: The newly-allowed up-to-three leading spaces before a `>` are untested in both regexes
samples.evidence: Both `BARE_BOX_RE` (checkbox-input.ts:9) and `QUOTE_RE` (list-commands.ts:45) gained a ` {0,3}` prefix, so `  > [ ]` / `  > - a` are now parsed as quoted lines while `    > - a` (four spaces, a code block) must not be. No test in checkbox-input.test.ts or list-commands.test.ts mounts a document with any space before the `>`; the boundary between 3 and 4 spaces — where a wrong answer rewrites a fenced/indented code block's contents — is entirely uncovered.

samples.summary: `taskItemText`'s empty-name fallback and the interactive (writable) aria-label path are untested
samples.evidence: `render` now writes `aria-label` for every checkbox, guarded by `if (name)` (preview.ts:377). The only new aria test ('names each checkbox after its own item text', preview.test.ts:64) constructs `new NotePreview()` with no `onToggleTask`, i.e. the read-only branch, and uses non-empty item text. Neither an empty task item (`- [ ]`, where `taskItemText` returns `''` and no attribute should be written) nor a preview constructed with `onToggleTask` is asserted to be labelled, even though the comment at preview.ts:53-55 claims the name is announced 'either way'.

samples.summary: The 'toggles a task item inside a blockquote' test likely passed before this change, so it does not cover the behaviour the diff alters
samples.evidence: The only preview.ts change is the aria-label loop; the task source-line tagging (`note-task-source-line`, preview.ts:61-71) reads `list_item_open.map` and is unaffected by blockquote nesting. The new test at preview.test.ts:111-121 asserts `toggles` is `[[0, true]]` for `> - [ ] quoted todo`, which the pre-change renderer already produced. It is presented as blockquote coverage but cannot fail if the blockquote work regresses — the real quoted-toggle logic lives in `setTaskChecked`, covered separately at list-commands.test.ts:276.
